Imo A main difference is ideally a more decentralized state and more power to businesses and cities over government. 

Mexicans arent a race, they are a nationality, so I wouldnt call this exactly "racism". Deportations and other policies are Lachman's policies, it doesnt mean his policies are what neo jeffersonianism itself (ideally) is. many other future presidents follow neo jeffersonianism in some shape or form but approach it differently. For example  Thang Levin is basically a Lachman fanboy but does ally the conservative party with the pro-mexican MLP.

Basically saying what lachman's policies are what neo jeffersonianism is is like basing communism off of leninism. You don't have to put "fascism" label on something if it is remotely comparable.
